newsitem.title: USA: St. Jude halts Cyberonics deal.
newsitem.headline: St. Jude halts Cyberonics deal.

text.p: St. Jude Medical Inc said it will not complete a proposed, $72-million acquisition of Cyberonics Inc.

The two had announced a merger agreement on April 8, 1996. "That agreement gave St. Jude Medical the option, but not the obligation, to complete the merger prior to October 18, 1996," St. Jude said late Wednesday.
Cyberonics' shareholders approved the agreement in July.
St. Jude said it maintains a minority ownership in Cyberonics.
The company could not immediately be reached for further explanation of the collapse of the deal.
Analysts said St. Jude probably pulled the plug because of problems with trial data on Cyberonics' implantable device for treating epilepsy by stimulating the vagus nerve.
"This implies that the data did not support the device," said J.P. Morgan Securities medical technology analyst Michael Weinstein.
Analysts said the announcement came as a surprise because management had been indicating the deal would go through.
In the long run, they said, halting the deal raises questions about St. Jude's diversification strategy.
"This means that St. Jude is not done diversifying" and likley will soon be making another strategic acquisition," Weinstein said.
St. Jude is the world's largest maker of heart valves and is a major manufacturer of pacemakers and other medical devices.
